transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lin (Redwood SE), Maya (Saltmarsh Head of ML), Marcus (Saltmarsh Platform), Priya (Saltmarsh SecOps), Alvaro (Saltmarsh CTO)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in, discuss capacity uplift options, EU VPC onboarding timeline, and confirm P99 latency SLOs and pilot benchmark dates. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, we've got about 40 minutes, main agenda — renewal timing, capacity uplifts for summer peak, and the EU + APAC ramp plan.
[00:18] Maya (Saltmarsh): thanks, yeah we wanna make sure we lock in commitments before our fiscal Q3 spend window, and we need to validate latency as we bring up the EU inference nodes.
[00:35] Diego (Redwood SE): quick note — we ran a sample on dedicated infra with the same model family you use, there was a measurable p99 bump at the long prompt tails, happy to go through config knobs.
[00:48] Marcus (Saltmarsh): when you say p99 bump, are we talking 300s of ms or seconds? We need hard numbers because our user-facing flows are sensitive.
[01:05] Diego: fair, I should say 300-450ms increase over p50 for long sequences in the test. With prefix KV caching and batching the p99 dropped back to ~120-180ms in the dedicated run.
[01:27] Priya (Saltmarsh): ok that's helpful. Security question first — will the EU VPC install use our KMS keys? We need full control of keys for PHI-ish data.
[01:40] Samira: yes — the private option supports customer-managed keys and HSM via our KMS integrations, we can share the integration checklist. We'll put that in the doc bundle.
[01:56] Alvaro (Saltmarsh): timeline is tight; we want EU in production for a pilot by mid July. Is that realistic for a VPC/private deployment?
[02:08] Lin (Redwood): doable if we start onboarding work immediately — there's a standard 3-week window for VPC peering, certs, and baseline smoke tests, then a week for performance tuning if you want dedicated GPUs.
[02:22] Maya: and pricing — we're evaluating committed reserved vs a hybrid commit+burst model. Our spike pattern is weekly with sharp peaks; we don't want to over-commit for idle capacity.
[02:35] Samira: understood. We can offer a tiered commit (base guaranteed throughput) + burst credits for transient spikes. For long-term extensions we can reduce unit price on the base. I'll share an example tier sheet.
[02:50] Marcus: also want to understand geographic failover — if EU capacity hits limits, can traffic fail over to hosted clusters with encryption in transit and audit logs?
[03:04] Diego: yes — smart routing supports region failover with fallback to compatible model variants. Fallback preserves TLS and audit logging; note there may be higher latency routing cross-region.
[03:18] Priya: are audit logs customer-visible in the console or do we stream them to our SIEM?
[03:26] Samira: both — we can retain logs in Redwood Console and push to your SIEM or S3 bucket, retention options are configurable. We'll include the retention matrix.
[03:40] Maya: okay on latency SLOs — we're targeting p95 <120ms and p99 <250ms for the majority of calls. Are those achievable with a dedicated pool in eu-west?
[03:54] Diego: For short-to-medium sequences yes; long-running, many-token narratives push p99 upward. We recommend enabling KV prefix caching and setting batching windows carefully. Also a slightly higher GPU class (A100x2 style) helps with fewer spikes.
[04:18] Marcus: what about quantization? We've been exploring int8 to reduce cost — does that materially affect latency or quality?
[04:30] Lin: quantization lowers memory and can reduce per-token compute, so cost drops; latency sometimes improves slightly but the big wins are reduced throughput pressure. Quality regressions depend on your prompts; we can run evals on your prompt suite.
[04:47] Maya: please do the evals — we have sensitive clinical prompts and we cannot degrade QA.
[04:54] Diego: we'll run a comparison: FP16 baseline, int8 static, and a ~mixed quant profile — report will show Rouge-like metrics and latency deltas.
[05:08] Samira: timeline check — renewal target is end of June to align with legal, but contract extension can be backdated to July 1 if needed. If you decide on dedicated capacity we'll need firm signal by June 11 to reserve the hardware for July.
[05:24] Alvaro: so June 11 is our soft deadline, understood.
[05:30] Maya: for the pilot benchmark, what inputs do you need from us?
[05:36] Diego: best is a tokenized sample set, 200 representative requests (mix of short and long), traffic histogram for qps and 99th percentile request size, and any specific prompt modification rules. Marcus can export that.
[05:50] Marcus: I can send the histogram and token mix, though some of the telemetry hangs in our old pipeline — will try to pull a 7-day window.
[05:59] Priya: on compliance, we need SOC2 Type II evidence, an ATO-ish network diagram, and confirmation of data-at-rest encryption and KMS key lifecycle.
[06:13] Samira: we'll attach SOC2 PDF, a sample network diagram for VPC peering, and the KMS workflow document in the security bundle.
[06:24] Maya: are there any cost impacts for streaming audit logs out to our S3?
[06:31] Samira: minimal — there is a small per-GB egress for log streaming if you route out of Redwood; though if you keep logs in-console it's included in your retention tier. We'll show comparisons in the doc.
[06:45] Diego: I'll call out a couple technical caveats — warm KV caches matter for p99 on long sessions; if you have many short ephemeral prompts cache hit rates drop and p99 suffers. Also continuous batching can trade a few ms for throughput; it's tunable.
[07:04] Marcus: can we pre-warm caches for scheduled batch jobs?
[07:08] Diego: yes, you can pin warm prefixes or schedule synthetic warm-up traffic.
[07:14] Marcus: great.
[07:16] Maya: one other ask — we want a canary policy for rolling updates that keeps a fraction of traffic on the previous model for 24 hours. Do you support A/B rollouts?
[07:26] Lin: yes, rollouts support weight-based canaries and automatic rollback on quality regressions if you supply eval checks. Redwood Optimize can monitor and alert on quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
[07:40] Samira: ok wrapping a bit into next steps — Diego we'll need the benchmark templates, Marcus you'll share telemetry, Priya you'll compile compliance contacts. We'll align dates for the pilot.
[07:54] Marcus: question about pricing — if we commit to a 12-month extension with a base commit and burst credits, do you offer a mid-term re-eval? Sometimes our usage grows faster.
[08:05] Samira: yes, contracts can include a mid-term cadence to revisit committed units and pricing thresholds. We can include scaling clauses.
[08:16] Alvaro: about fallback — if we fall back to hosted region during EU outage, are we subject to different data residency terms? We can't send clinical data offshore for certain workflows.
[08:29] Priya: this is critical — we have flow-level routing rules, some flows must never leave EU.
[08:36] Lin: we can implement route policies that mark certain endpoints as 'EU-only' and not failover those to hosted clusters. For non-sensitive traffic we can allow cross-region fallback.
[08:50] Maya: ok that solves it.
[08:52] Diego: I'll document the routing policy options and sample config for flow tagging.
[08:58] Samira: good — I'll attach that to the security bundle.
[09:02] Maya: on the pilot and benchmarks — can we see a sample report from a previous customer similar size? Not full PII obviously but a template.
[09:12] Samira: yes, we'll redact and share a sample benchmark readout plus the runbook.
[09:19] Marcus: if the pilot shows p99 above 250ms, what mitigation steps are on the table?
[09:26] Diego: we have options: enable prefix caching, bump GPU class, increase pooling (more workers), change quantization profile to higher precision, and tune batching latency window. Some are infra changes, some are config. We'll prioritize least-disruptive.
[09:41] Maya: how long does a hardware bump take in an activation window?
[09:45] Lin: if you have a dedicated reservation we can re-provision within a week; otherwise hardware scheduling plus procurement could be longer. So earlier commit is better.
[09:58] Alvaro: let's be aggressive — we want the EU pilot 6/15 as proposed by Samira.
[10:05] Samira: noted — I'll draft a proposed timeline: 6/9 receive telemetry + prompt set, 6/11 final decision on commit, 6/12 start VPC peering, 6/15 pilot benchmark run, 6/22 staging validation, 7/01 production activation.
[10:26] Maya: that timeline sounds fine but we may need to nudge a day on the telemetry export.
[10:31] Marcus: I'll aim for June 10 but might be June 11.
[10:35] Priya: I'll try to get the compliance contacts sooner (6/09 ok).
[10:40] Samira: perfect. Anything else?
[10:43] Maya: one minor thing — can you provide a template for the contract amendment language for a rolling commit? Our legal likes to see language in advance.
[10:51] Samira: yes, legal will share an amendment template. I'll include that in the next email.
[10:58] Diego: also note our dedicated pools have SLA-backed throughput and we can include latency credits for sustained SLA misses — I'll include SLA language in the package.
[11:10] Alvaro: good.
[11:12] Samira: quick recap of next steps and owners: Samira sends pricing + contract amendment + security bundle; Diego runs benchmarks and shares runbook; Marcus sends telemetry and prompt set; Priya provides compliance contacts; schedule pilot for 2026-06-15. Any objections?
[11:30] Maya: none, sounds good.
[11:32] Marcus: yep.
[11:33] Priya: good.
[11:35] Samira: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription conflated a few names early (Samira vs Samara) and sometimes labeled speakers as Speaker 1/2 in source — we corrected most but left a few small artifacts.
